messages.author: 556b672b7e68700f
messages.subject: Concurvity
parts:
Hi all,

Let f(x) be the spatial term in the model, and f(d) is another term I want to estimate. Now suppose d is a function of x.

In the world of GAMs (mgcv), if I try to estimate f(x) and f(d) in a model, those terms would be concurved. This makes estimation of the smoothing parameters potentially unstable and problematic for inference. 

In the setting of R-INLA, are there potential problems with estimating two model terms that may potentially be concurved in the sense above? To be concrete, I will model f(x) with an SPDE model, and f(d) with a RW2 model.  

Best,

W

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Concurvity
parts:
the problems of this type will not go away, but priors will make it more
'stable'

here is a small example (from your description), you'll see the fit is
good although the marginal uncertainty in each component is huge (which
is a sign that something is going on)

n <- 100
x <- (1:n)/n
f1 <- x+sin(10*x)
f2 <- exp(f1)
s <- 0.01
y <- f1 + f2 + rnorm(n, sd = s)

r <- inla(y ~ 1 + f(x, model = "rw2") + f(xx, model = "rw2"),
data = data.frame(x = x, xx = x, y = y),
control.family = list(
hyper = list(prec = list(initial = log(1/s^2),
fixed = TRUE))),
verbose = TRUE)
